description: A 2×2 composite of four TEM bright-field micrographs, all from the same material: the 15Mn5Ni low-density steel in the HR+CR+1173 K condition, after tensile deformation to true strains labelled ε~0.02, ε~0.05 and ε~0.14. A shared label "15Mn5Ni" spans the top, and the vertical label "HR+CR+1173 K" runs down the left of panels (a) and (c). Every panel carries a 200 nm scale bar at its lower-left/lower-right. (a) (ε~0.02) shows a relatively clean austenite grain traversed by individual dislocations that bow, loop and tangle around two dark elongated elliptical particles (identified in the caption as B2 particles), i.e. dislocation–particle interaction. (b) (ε~0.05) shows marked dislocation multiplication: dense, tangled and partly planar dislocation arrays filling the grain with only local banding. (c) and (d) (both ε~0.14) show a strongly refined, cross-hatched planar slip-band structure, with (c) containing a bright elongated particle within the heavily banded matrix. The figure demonstrates, as a function of increasing strain, the sequence from dislocation–particle interaction and dislocation multiplication to slip-band refinement in the deformed 15Mn5Ni austenite; no numerical values other than strain labels and scale bars are printed.

observations.observation: All four panels are TEM bright-field micrographs with a 200 nm scale bar, belonging to the 15Mn5Ni alloy in the HR+CR+1173 K condition.
Panel (a) is labelled ε~0.02 and shows dislocations bowing and tangling around dark elongated elliptical particles, described in the caption as dislocation-B2 particle interaction.
The caption states that (a) indicates dislocation-B2 particle interaction and (b-d) show dislocation multiplication and refinement of slip bands with strain.
Panel (b) is labelled ε~0.05 and shows a pronounced increase in dislocation density with tangled and partly planar dislocation arrangements relative to (a).
Panels (c) and (d) are both labelled ε~0.14 and show closely spaced, cross-hatched planar slip bands, i.e. a refined substructure at the highest strain.
Only strain labels (ε~0.02, ε~0.05, ε~0.14) and 200 nm scale bars are printed; no numeric band-spacing values appear in the figure.
The citing text reports that non-shearable B2 particles were noticed as obstacles to dislocation motion and thereby caused early initiation of slip band refinement.

The citing text states that inhomogeneous slip band spacing developed in Ni-containing LDS alloys (which includes 15Mn5Ni), whereas the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni alloy exhibited homogeneous slip band spacing under HR+CR+1173 K conditions.

The citing text describes progressive substructure evolution from dislocation multiplication to planar slip activity and then slip band refinement with applied strain in the recrystallized, precipitate-free austenite grains.
A mean slip band spacing of ~200 ± 30 nm is stated in the citing text, but that value refers to fine κ-carbide-containing regions of 28Mn0Ni and is not a measurement of this figure.
The figure is a post-tensile-deformation study: specimens were interrupted at the labelled strains rather than tested to failure.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field image, 200 nm scale bar, ε~0.02: individual dislocations bowing, looping and tangling around two dark elongated elliptical particles (caption: B2 particles) in an otherwise fairly clean austenite matrix — dislocation–B2 particle interaction.
TEM bright-field image, 200 nm scale bar, ε~0.05: dense tangled and partly planar dislocation arrays filling the area, interpreted as dislocation multiplication with early band formation.

TEM bright-field image, 200 nm scale bar, ε~0.14: heavily banded matrix with fine intersecting planar slip bands plus a bright elongated particle; caption attributes this to refinement of slip bands with strain.
TEM bright-field image, 200 nm scale bar, ε~0.14: cross-hatched, closely spaced planar slip-band structure of high density, i.e. refined slip bands at the highest applied strain.
